title: Workload Business Continuity: Stay Online and Secure
summary: Outages shouldn't mean going dark or going unprotected. See how Business Continuity Cloud keeps workloads connected and inspected, with no manual cutover.
body_markdown:
Enterprises should evaluate disaster recovery solutions using four criteria: operational independence, automated failover, policy consistency, and testability. The best solution will run on geographically separated infrastructure that doesn’t depend on the primary cloud or its admin portal. It should automatically redirect traffic to meet the organization’s recovery time objective (RTO), enforce the same policies on the backup path, and allow failover validation without production disruptions. Zscaler Business Continuity Cloud for workloads delivers all four capabilities.


No, Zscaler Business Continuity Cloud doesn’t involve manual cutover. Failover to the private service edge is automatic, and no scripts run mid-incident. Provisioning uses existing licensing and configuration lives in one place, rather than being repeated across each gateway.


Yes, Zscaler customers can pre-configure a DNX TXT record that Cloud Connector polls periodically. This gives customers an external switch to trigger failover, even when the admin portal isn’t reachable.


Yes, Zscaler customers can run self-service fire drills on defined subsets of traffic on a regular cadence, all without redirecting all production traffic or waiting on Zscaler. This way, teams can validate that the failover path works before it’s needed.


Yes, Zscaler customers can fail over to the Zscaler-managed Business Continuity Cloud or to Zscaler Virtual or Private Service Edges in their own data centers. For customers in regulated industries, this gives auditors and boards a defined failover path that can be validated on a schedule. It also gives them a control mechanism that works even if the admin portal is unavailable.


Traditional disaster recovery plans have a major focus on data replication and system restoration, but cloud workload recovery plans need a focus on secure path transit. During outages, traffic often falls back to legacy VPNs or uninspected public routing, which introduces a major security gap. True continuity requires inline zero trust enforcement that is consistently applied, even during failover scenarios.


If a security system fails open, that means that it bypasses security controls to maintain operational uptime and therefore leaves workloads unprotected from threats. This design choice prioritizes availability over security so that uninspected, potentially malicious traffic is allowed into corporate networks during outages. Zero trust continuity addresses the risks of systems failing open, and ensures active protection is applied inline.
